title: Mapilak banana (NSIC Bn 01): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Mapilak banana: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Mapilak banana is a banana variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Mapilak is a registered banana variety, also sold or known as NSIC Bn 01. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2017 as NSIC 2017 Bn 01. Institute of Plant Breeding bred it. Its record notes a yield of 12.96 kg.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Bn 01, this is the same banana. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [banana variety finder](/crop-varieties/banana), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [banana farming in the Philippines](/crops/banana-farming-philippines).

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. Its record notes a yield of 12.96 kg. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit banana fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Banana aphid](/pests/banana-aphid), [Banana bunchy top](/diseases/banana-bunchy-top), [Banana weevil](/pests/banana-weevil), [black sigatoka](/diseases/black-sigatoka). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A fruit of Mapilak weighs about 115.35 grams, and its shape is slightly curve to straight. The flesh is yellow orange and firm.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Fingers about 14 cm, 115 g, yellow to orange skin, yellow orange firm sweet flesh.
Resistant to banana bunchy top virus and its aphid vector.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: iPB's dessert banana bred to resist bunchy top, the first banana with an NSIC number. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Mapilak banana

Lakatan and latundan sell fresh, saba goes to cooking and banana cue, and Cavendish goes to export. Fusarium wilt and bunchy top end many farms, so plant clean tissue cultured plantlets, and a tolerant selection where wilt is known. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for banana](/land-preparation/banana-land-preparation).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Bn 01 the same as Mapilak?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Bn 01 is another name for Mapilak, registered as NSIC 2017 Bn 01. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 12.96 kg. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Mapilak?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
